back: The energy a person gets from food each day, in kilocalories (kcal); adults need very roughly 2,000-2,500 kcal.
An unbalanced diet: too little of some nutrients (undernutrition) or too much energy (obesity).
The distance food travels from where it is produced to where it is eaten.
Large-scale commercial farming, often controlled by companies that also process, transport and sell food.
Highest in HICs (often above about 3,000 kcal); lowest in parts of sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia and in conflict zones.

front: Reasons for variation in calorie intake
back: Income, food production methods, climate and hazards, conflict, population growth, infrastructure and diet.
Population growth, rising incomes (more meat and dairy), urbanisation (processed food), global tastes.

front: Reasons for the globalisation of food
back: Refrigerated containers and air freight, demand for year-round produce, cheap production in LICs, supermarkets and TNCs, lower tariffs.
From the 1960s: high-yielding varieties of wheat and rice with fertiliser, pesticides and irrigation, raising yields in Asia and Latin America.
